previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute watery diarrhea and hypoxia. He had been evaluated earlier the same day for Foley catheter discomfort, but his urinalysis was unremarkable. Shortly after discharge, he developed multiple episodes of non-bloody diarrhea and worsening shortness of breath. In the ED, he was found to have oxygen saturation dropping to 90-92% on room air. A chest X-ray revealed a right lower lobe opacity, suspicious for pneumonia. He was started on IV levofloxacin and admitted. Diarrhea resolved spontaneously, and stool studies for C. diff, ova and parasites, and bacterial pathogens were negative. Blood cultures showed no growth. His oxygen levels improved, and he was weaned off supplemental oxygen. He completed a course of antibiotics and was discharged home with instructions to finish oral levofloxacin, obtain a follow-up chest X-ray, and attend scheduled urology and primary care appointments. His chronic conditions remained stable.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with CAD s/p CABG in ___, AVR (aortic valve

vs. PND, vs. PNA, vs. psychogenic pain. 
.
#Chest pain:  When patient arrived to the floor he reported Left 
sided chest pain.  Given his history of CAD s/p CABG he was 
evaluated as high risk for MI. Patient was given aspirin in the 
ED, but no Oxygen, morphine, or SNL. Due to risk of MI, CE were 
sent in the ED. Enzymes negative except for slightly elevated 
Trop-T at 0.04 (below his baseline). EKG in ED unchanged from 
prior. Old RBBB. Due to these negative findings. We continued to 
cycle Cardiac enzymes to rule out MI.  ___ round of enzymes were 
also negative at 12 hours.   D dimer was tested due to 
possibility of PE.  D dimer result was normal and PE was ruled 
out.   Psychogenic pain was considered the most likely on the 
diagnosis given past medical hx and previous notes written by 
PCP and other physicians.  However, due to history of CAD and 
CABG patient should follow up with PCP and an outpatient stress 
test should be arranged.  Patient was given instructions to 
follow up with his PCP ___ 2 weeks.   
.
# Depression: Patient was continued on home dose of celexa (40 
mg). He should continue on this dose after discharge.  He should 
follow up with his PCP to discuss dose of medication and his 
participation in therapy.  
.
# Chronic urinary retention:  Patient was continued on 
indwelling Foley.  Patient disconnected foley catheter overnight 
and a new catheter was put in.  Patient will be discharged to 
home with catheter.
.
 #DMII - Patient was continued on diabetic diet while in house.  
No medications taken at home.  QID finger sticks were performed 
and patient was maintained on insulin sliding scale while an 
inpatient.  Patient should resume a diabetic diet while at home 
and should follow up with PCP to discuss possibility of starting 
medications to better help control his diabetes.  
.
#HTN -  Patient was given metoprolol 50mg bid.  He will be 
discharged on his home dose of 50mg Atenolol daily. 
.
#Hyperlipidemia - Patient was continued on 80mg atorvastatin.  
He should continue taking this dose after discharge.
